reply.text: Russia's condition to withhold support for the envoy appointment without de facto authority agreement was not adopted, as the final clause mandates consultation but omits any consent requirement.

Ghana's statement proposed a Special Envoy as a complement to UNAMA's work, which the adopted clause implemented by requesting the Secretary-General's appointment after consultations, without imposing a consent requirement.
Ghana's proposal for a Special Envoy as a complement to UNAMA was adopted as a request for an envoy with expertise to advance recommendations while preserving UNAMA's mandate.

EARLY: Russia expected consultation with the de facto authorities and consideration of all Council members' views.
LATE: Paragraph 3 asks the Secretary-General to appoint an envoy after consulting Council members, relevant Afghan actors including authorities, women and civil society, the region and the wider international community.
LINK: Russia demanded de facto authority consent for the envoy, but the adopted clause mandates consultation with relevant Afghan actors while omitting any consent requirement.
